Q0107

“It is impossible to think of anything at all in the world,…” — Immanuel Kant (Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals. Theme: freedom.

Quotes / Immanuel Kant / Q0107

English

It is impossible to think of anything at all in the world, or indeed even beyond it, that could be considered good without limitation except a good will.
Thinker Immanuel Kant
School Critical Philosophy
Source Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals
Theme Freedom

About Immanuel Kant

Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) spent nearly his entire life in Königsberg, rising from tutor to professor at the university there. After early scientific and metaphysical essays, the Critique of Pure Reason (1781/1787) launched his “critical” philosophy.

How to read this passage

Philosophers distinguish several ideas under the single word freedom. Negative freedom emphasizes non-interference; positive freedom emphasizes the capacity to act according to reasons, virtue, or authentic desire. This passage enters that discussion through freedom, morality.

Concepts in this quote

Freedom
Freedom is among the most searched and most contested themes in philosophy: what it is to choose, to be responsible, and to live without illegitimate constraint.
Morality
Morality in philosophy concerns right and wrong, obligation, and the standards by which we judge persons and acts.
